runs.title: Continuity smoke test
runs.summary: The prior local runner still compiles and runs on Windows with GCC 16.1 and sorts 1,000 uint32 keys correctly. Not an evaluation of the goal.
runs.how: Checked that the benchmark runner from the earlier local research still builds with the current Windows compiler (GCC 16.1) and sorts correctly.
runs.how_es: Comprobó que el banco de pruebas de la investigación local anterior sigue compilando con el compilador actual de Windows (GCC 16.1) y ordena correctamente.

runs.title: Viability review and repository reset
runs.summary: Judged the original goal (25% faster in 90% of a large benchmark matrix) very unlikely to be reached, replaced it with an open search for new mechanisms and archived the prior research.
runs.how: Reviewed whether the original goal (25% faster in 90% of a large matrix of cases) was reachable after 72 earlier experiments. It was judged very unlikely, so the goal became an open search for a genuinely new mechanism, and six starting ideas were written down.
runs.how_es: Revisó si el objetivo original (un 25 % más rápido en el 90 % de una gran matriz de casos) era alcanzable tras 72 experimentos previos. Se consideró muy improbable, así que el objetivo pasó a ser una búsqueda abierta de un mecanismo realmente nuevo y se anotaron seis ideas de partida.

runs.title: Record permutation headroom pilot
runs.summary: Gathering the payload takes 51–68% of an indirect sort of 64- and 128-byte records, so a permutation as cheap as a sequential copy would give about 1.3–1.4×. Enough room to try a candidate, with little margin.
runs.result: 1.29–1.40× estimated headroom; 5/8 cases ≥1.3× on both seeds
runs.baseline: fastest of vqsort + gather, x86-simd-sort + gather and pdqsort on rows
runs.how: Sorting wide records (64 or 128 bytes each) is usually done in two steps: sort small (key, position) pairs, then gather every record into its new place. The gather jumps all over memory. This pilot measured how much of the total time that gather takes, to see whether a smarter way of moving records could pay off.
runs.compared_with: vqsort plus gather, x86-simd-sort plus gather, and pdqsort sorting the whole rows.
runs.faster_where: The gather is 51–68% of the time. If moving records cost no more than a straight copy, sorting would be 1.29–1.40× faster. 5 of 8 cases reach 1.3× on both seeds: enough room to try a real candidate, with little margin.
runs.title_es: Margen en la permutación de registros
runs.how_es: Ordenar registros anchos (64 o 128 bytes cada uno) suele hacerse en dos pasos: ordenar pares pequeños (clave, posición) y después recoger cada registro en su nuevo sitio. Esa recogida salta por toda la memoria. Este piloto midió cuánto tiempo se lleva, para ver si una forma más lista de mover registros podría compensar.
runs.compared_with_es: vqsort más recogida, x86-simd-sort más recogida, y pdqsort ordenando las filas completas.
runs.faster_where_es: La recogida es el 51–68 % del tiempo. Si mover registros costara lo mismo que una copia secuencial, ordenar sería 1,29–1,40× más rápido. 5 de 8 casos llegan a 1,3× con ambas semillas: hay margen para probar un candidato real, aunque justo.

runs.title: Blocked record permutation probe
runs.summary: Rewriting and sorting descriptors and then moving the records in cache-sized tiles took 1.67–2.14× as long as the original gather phase. The probe measured those costs together. Gather with software prefetch won all 48 paired repetitions.
runs.baseline: fastest measured reference, including gather with software prefetch
opens: gather with software prefetch as the control to beat
runs.how: After sorting, split the output into 256 KiB tiles that fit in the CPU’s L2 cache. Inside each tile, sort the requests by where each record comes from, so reads move forward through memory, then write every record straight to its final slot.
runs.compared_with: The fastest measured reference, including a plain gather with software prefetch (asking the CPU to load rows a little ahead of time).
runs.faster_where: Slower in every case: 0.54–0.65× (0 of 8 cases at 1.3×). Sorting the requests cost more than the better locality saved. The simple prefetching gather won all 48 paired runs.
runs.how_es: Tras ordenar, dividir la salida en bloques de 256 KiB que caben en la caché L2 del procesador. Dentro de cada bloque, ordenar las peticiones según de dónde viene cada registro, para leer la memoria hacia delante, y escribir cada registro directamente en su sitio final.
runs.compared_with_es: La referencia más rápida medida, incluida una recogida simple con prefetch por software (pedir al procesador que cargue las filas un poco antes).
runs.faster_where_es: Más lento en todos los casos: 0,54–0,65× (0 de 8 casos llegan a 1,3×). Ordenar las peticiones costó más de lo que ahorró leer en orden. La recogida simple con prefetch ganó las 48 repeticiones emparejadas.

runs.title: Page-remapped merge pilot
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.summary: Mapping pages instead of copying them pays off from 64 KiB extents upwards (4 KiB extents lose). In a merge only page-aligned slices qualify, which was 37.5% of the output when two runs overlap at the edges and 3–7% for bursty runs.
runs.result: 1.52–1.59× estimated for edge overlap; at most 1.08× for bursty runs
runs.how: When two sorted runs are merged, long stretches of the output come from only one of them. Instead of copying those bytes, ask the operating system to map the same physical memory pages into the output, so no data moves. This pilot measured what a remap costs compared with a copy, and how many pages a merge could reuse.
runs.compared_with: Copying with memcpy into a new buffer; a plain two-finger merge and a galloping merge that copies stretches in bulk.
runs.faster_where: Remapping beats copying for blocks of 64 KiB and up; 4 KiB blocks lose. Estimated 1.52–1.59× when the runs overlap only at their edges, but at most 1.08× when the runs alternate in bursts.
runs.title_es: Piloto de mezcla con remapeo de páginas
runs.how_es: Al mezclar dos tramos ordenados, largas partes de la salida vienen de uno solo. En vez de copiar esos bytes, se pide al sistema operativo que mapee las mismas páginas de memoria física en la salida, sin mover datos. Este piloto midió cuánto cuesta remapear frente a copiar y cuántas páginas podría reutilizar una mezcla.
runs.compared_with_es: Copiar con memcpy a un buffer nuevo; una mezcla clásica de dos punteros y una mezcla con búsqueda galopante que copia tramos en bloque.
runs.faster_where_es: Remapear gana a copiar a partir de bloques de 64 KiB; con 4 KiB pierde. Estimación: 1,52–1,59× cuando los tramos solo se solapan en los extremos, pero como mucho 1,08× cuando se alternan a ráfagas.

runs.title: Page-remapped merge candidate
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.summary: Mapping aligned input pages into the output beat the best fresh-output merge of two sorted runs of 128-byte records by 1.33–1.36×, and by 2.67× when 75% of the output was mapped. It lost to a merge into an already-touched buffer (0.36–0.74×) and regressed on bursty and interleaved runs (0.82–0.86×). Synthetic data only.
runs.result: 1.326–2.668× on edge-overlap runs (2/4 cases ≥1.3×, 0/4 ≥1.5× on both seeds)
runs.baseline: fastest merge into a fresh output
opens: frequency of mappable pages in real sorted batches
runs.how: The real implementation: walk the merge, map every page-aligned stretch of at least 64 KiB into the output, and copy the leftovers. The caller sees an ordinary contiguous, read-only array.
runs.compared_with: The fastest merge into a fresh output (plain, galloping bulk copy, and a hybrid). Also, separately, a merge into an output buffer that already exists in memory.
runs.faster_where: 1.33–1.36× faster on runs that overlap at the edges, and 2.67× when 75% of the output can be mapped. Slower than writing into a buffer that is already in memory (0.36–0.74×), and slower on bursty or interleaved runs (0.82–0.86×). Synthetic data only.
runs.title_es: Candidato de mezcla con remapeo de páginas
runs.how_es: La implementación real: recorrer la mezcla, mapear en la salida cada tramo alineado a página de al menos 64 KiB y copiar el resto. Quien la usa ve un array normal, contiguo y de solo lectura.
runs.compared_with_es: La mezcla más rápida hacia una salida nueva (clásica, galopante con copia en bloque e híbrida). Y, aparte, una mezcla hacia un buffer de salida que ya está en memoria.
runs.faster_where_es: 1,33–1,36× más rápido con tramos que se solapan en los extremos, y 2,67× cuando se puede mapear el 75 % de la salida. Más lento que escribir en un buffer que ya está en memoria (0,36–0,74×) y con tramos a ráfagas o intercalados (0,82–0,86×). Solo datos sintéticos.

runs.title: GH Archive page coverage
runs.summary: All eight registered archive pairs had disjoint event-time ranges. Between 48.25% and nearly 100% of the modeled bytes can be remapped, so these inputs measure assembly of preordered ranges and leave overlap untested.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.result: 8/8 pairs passed 37.5% coverage; 0/8 had timestamp overlap
opens: timing against two bulk copies on the archive batch sizes
runs.how: Does real data have long one-sided stretches? Took 8 pairs of consecutive hourly batches of public GitHub events (1.6 million events) and counted how many bytes a merge could remap instead of copy.
runs.compared_with: Nothing timed: this run measures the shape of real data.
runs.faster_where: 48–100% of the bytes could be remapped. But the hours never overlapped in time, so this only tests gluing batches that are already in order, not a real interleaved merge.
runs.title_es: Cobertura de páginas en GH Archive
runs.how_es: ¿Tienen los datos reales tramos largos de un solo lado? Se tomaron 8 pares de lotes horarios consecutivos de eventos públicos de GitHub (1,6 millones de eventos) y se contó cuántos bytes podría remapear una mezcla en vez de copiarlos.
runs.compared_with_es: Nada cronometrado: este run mide la forma de los datos reales.
runs.faster_where_es: Se podría remapear el 48–100 % de los bytes. Pero las horas nunca se solaparon en el tiempo, así que solo prueba unir lotes que ya vienen en orden, no una mezcla real intercalada.

runs.title: Page remapping on GH Archive batch sizes
runs.summary: On eight disjoint pairs with batch sizes and order derived from GH Archive, remapping beat every fresh-output reference. It beat the resident-buffer references in the two cases where almost all pages could be mapped. Real overlapping arrivals remain untested.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.baseline: fastest of scalar, galloping bulk, hybrid and two-copy concatenation for fresh output; hybrid and two-copy concatenation for resident output
opens: test overlapping batches from a source with independent arrival and event clocks
runs.how: Timed the remapping approach on the 8 real batch sizes and orders from GH Archive (with synthetic keys and payloads), against every reasonable way of building a fresh output, including simply concatenating with two memcpy calls.
runs.compared_with: Fresh output: plain, galloping and hybrid merges and a two-copy concatenation. Separately: hybrid and two-copy into a buffer that already exists in memory.
runs.faster_where: 1.43–1.66× faster when about half the pages can be mapped, and 6.7–7.3× when almost all can (7 of 8 cases at 1.5×). Against a buffer already in memory it only wins in the two nearly fully mapped pairs (1.66–1.74×); otherwise 0.38–0.49×. Only batches that do not overlap in time were tested.
runs.title_es: Remapeo de páginas con lotes de GH Archive
runs.how_es: Se cronometró el remapeo con los 8 tamaños y órdenes de lote reales de GH Archive (con claves y contenido sintéticos), frente a todas las formas razonables de construir una salida nueva, incluida concatenar con dos llamadas a memcpy.
runs.compared_with_es: Salida nueva: mezclas clásica, galopante e híbrida y concatenación con dos copias. Aparte: híbrida y dos copias hacia un buffer que ya está en memoria.
runs.faster_where_es: 1,43–1,66× más rápido cuando se puede mapear cerca de la mitad de las páginas, y 6,7–7,3× cuando casi todas (7 de 8 casos llegan a 1,5×). Frente a un buffer que ya está en memoria solo gana en los dos pares casi totalmente mapeables (1,66–1,74×); en el resto, 0,38–0,49×. Solo se probaron lotes que no se solapan en el tiempo.

runs.title: Record permutation by source band
runs.summary: Grouping reads by source band took about 23% longer on the primary batch. Preparing the groups and moving rows together took longer than reading ahead in the original layout.
runs.baseline: Fastest measured indirect sort with software prefetch
runs.how: A cheaper version of the tile idea. Instead of sorting the requests in each output window, group them with a histogram by which part of the input they read from. Then read each input band in order and write the rows into the window.
runs.compared_with: The fastest indirect sort with software prefetch (vqsort or x86-simd-sort, with and without streaming stores) and ska_sort on whole rows.
runs.faster_where: About 23% slower on 8 million 16-byte records (0.81×), and slower in all 6 cells. Preparing the groups and moving rows took longer than just reading ahead in the original layout.
runs.title_es: Permutación de registros por bandas de origen
runs.how_es: Una versión más barata de la idea por bloques. En vez de ordenar las peticiones de cada ventana de salida, se agrupan con un histograma según la parte de la entrada de la que leen. Después se lee cada banda de entrada en orden y se escriben las filas en la ventana.
runs.compared_with_es: La ordenación indirecta más rápida con prefetch por software (vqsort o x86-simd-sort, con y sin escrituras en streaming) y ska_sort sobre filas completas.
runs.faster_where_es: Alrededor de un 23 % más lento con 8 millones de registros de 16 bytes (0,81×), y más lento en las 6 celdas. Preparar los grupos y mover las filas tardó más que simplemente leer por adelantado en el orden original.

runs.title: Windows page remapping and first read
runs.summary: For 64 KiB blocks, Windows remapping and a first read took 2.21–2.54× the time of streaming copy and a first read. The first access to the new virtual addresses dominated even when larger blocks made the remap calls fast.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.baseline: AVX2 streaming copy plus first sweep into a reused output
closes: Windows placeholder remapping for the measured contract
runs.how: The same remapping idea, ported to Windows APIs, for reassembling 256 MiB of sorted runs into one contiguous output.
runs.compared_with: An AVX2 streaming copy into a reused buffer, followed by the same first read.
runs.faster_where: 2.2–2.5× slower with 64 KiB blocks (0.39–0.45×). Even with 2 MiB blocks, where remapping itself took under 1 ms, the first touch of the new addresses cost about 83 ms. Closes Windows remapping for this case; the Linux results stand.
runs.how_es: La misma idea de remapeo, llevada a las APIs de Windows, para reunir 256 MiB de tramos ordenados en una sola salida contigua.
runs.compared_with_es: Una copia en streaming con AVX2 a un buffer reutilizado, seguida de la misma primera lectura.
runs.faster_where_es: 2,2–2,5× más lento con bloques de 64 KiB (0,39–0,45×). Incluso con bloques de 2 MiB, donde el remapeo en sí tardó menos de 1 ms, el primer acceso a las nuevas direcciones costó unos 83 ms. Cierra el remapeo en Windows para este caso; los resultados en Linux se mantienen.

runs.title: Stable rank inversion for four-record groups
runs.summary: Computing ranks and inverting them in AVX2 registers took 5–37% longer than the fastest direct SIMD reference on the primary batches. The extra work still cost time in the cache-resident control.
runs.idea: 5. Exact rank computation without data movement
runs.baseline: Best of the direct AVX2 compare-exchange network and shuffle lookup
runs.how: For millions of tiny groups of 4 records: compute each record’s final position (its rank) with a few vector comparisons, then turn the ranks into a shuffle, two groups at a time inside AVX2 registers. Every record is written exactly once, with no partitioning.
runs.compared_with: A direct AVX2 sorting network, a published shuffle-lookup method (Mimicry), and vqsort and x86-simd-sort called per group.
runs.faster_where: It beat the library calls, but was 5–37% slower than the direct AVX2 network (0.73–0.95×), even with the data in cache. Building the shuffle from the ranks takes a chain of steps that costs too much.
runs.title_es: Inversión de rangos en grupos de cuatro
runs.how_es: Para millones de grupos diminutos de 4 registros: calcular la posición final de cada registro (su rango) con unas pocas comparaciones vectoriales y convertir los rangos en una permutación, dos grupos a la vez dentro de registros AVX2. Cada registro se escribe una sola vez, sin particionar.
runs.compared_with_es: Una red de ordenación AVX2 directa, un método publicado de tabla de permutaciones (Mimicry), y vqsort y x86-simd-sort llamados por grupo.
runs.faster_where_es: Ganó a las llamadas a librería, pero fue un 5–37 % más lento que la red AVX2 directa (0,73–0,95×), incluso con los datos en caché. Construir la permutación a partir de los rangos exige una cadena de pasos que cuesta demasiado.

runs.title: Page reuse in completed taxi-trip batches
runs.summary: Only one of twelve weekly pairs overlapped in pickup time. Four rows of that pair fell inside the overlap, and choosing the output offset did not increase its page reuse.
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.result: 1/12 weekly pairs overlapped and 0/12 put at least 5% of rows in the overlap
closes: small seaborn taxi sample for overlapping merge timing
opens: dense completed-trip replay with substantial overlap
runs.how: Looked for real data where batches do overlap in time: NYC taxi trips grouped by drop-off day and sorted by pickup time. Counted how many pages a merge could reuse, and whether shifting where the output starts helps.
runs.compared_with: Nothing timed: this run measures the shape of real data.
runs.faster_where: Only 1 of 12 weekly pairs overlapped, with just 4 rows inside the overlap (0.14%). The sample is too sparse; a denser real source is needed before timing a real overlapping merge.
runs.title_es: Reutilización de páginas en lotes de taxis
runs.how_es: Se buscaron datos reales donde los lotes sí se solapan en el tiempo: viajes de taxi de Nueva York agrupados por día de llegada y ordenados por hora de recogida. Se contó cuántas páginas podría reutilizar una mezcla y si ayuda desplazar el inicio de la salida.
runs.compared_with_es: Nada cronometrado: este run mide la forma de los datos reales.
runs.faster_where_es: Solo 1 de 12 pares semanales se solapó, con apenas 4 filas dentro del solape (0,14 %). La muestra es demasiado escasa; hace falta una fuente real más densa antes de cronometrar una mezcla con solape real.

runs.title: Bandwidth screen for three-byte sorting keys
runs.summary: With eight workers, a transfer-only estimate including conversion reached 1.086–1.178×. All four primary cases missed the 1.30× gate before any sorting work was charged.
runs.model: Codex (exact model and reasoning settings not captured)
runs.idea: 2. Compressed keys in flight for bandwidth-bound regimes
runs.baseline: fastest of memcpy and AVX2 streaming copy at full width
closes: 24-bit width savings alone with up to two intervening memory transfers
runs.how: A bucket can remember the first byte of every key it contains. Store the other three bytes between passes and rebuild the full keys at the end.
runs.compared_with: Measured sequential copies of four-byte and three-byte keys on the same cores. Used measured encoding and decoding times in the estimate.
runs.faster_where: With eight cores, moving already packed keys was 1.166–1.331× as fast. Including both conversions and two intervening transfers brought the estimate to 1.086–1.178×. The experiment timed memory movement and conversion.
runs.title_es: Prueba de ancho de banda con claves de tres bytes
runs.how_es: Una cubeta puede recordar el primer byte de todas sus claves. Entre pasadas se guardan los otros tres bytes y al final se reconstruyen las claves completas.
runs.compared_with_es: Se midieron copias secuenciales de claves de cuatro y tres bytes en los mismos núcleos. La estimación incluye los tiempos medidos de compresión y reconstrucción.
runs.faster_where_es: Con ocho núcleos, copiar claves ya comprimidas fue entre 1,166 y 1,331 veces más rápido. Al sumar ambas conversiones y dos transferencias intermedias, la estimación quedó entre 1,086× y 1,178×. Se midieron transferencias y conversiones.

runs.title: Helper-thread prefetch for scattered records
runs.summary: The best helper took 180–182 ms on two threads of one core. Giving each thread half the output took 102–114 ms for the same 256 MiB permutation.
runs.model: Codex (exact model and reasoning settings not captured)
runs.baseline: fastest of seven split gathers on the same two hardware threads
closes: 128-byte random gather with a bounded prefetch helper
runs.how: One thread copies all the records. A second thread looks ahead in the destination order and asks the CPU to bring the next records into cache.
runs.compared_with: Seven methods using the same two hardware threads to copy one half each, including in-thread prefetch and stores that bypass cache.
runs.faster_where: On the two 256 MiB permutations with threads sharing one core, the best helper took 59–77% longer than the fastest split. It did beat the single-worker control by 1.16–1.46×. The benchmark measures copying in the supplied order.
runs.title_es: Hilo auxiliar para precargar registros dispersos
runs.how_es: Un hilo copia todos los registros. El segundo lee por adelantado el orden de salida y solicita al procesador que cargue los próximos registros en caché.
runs.compared_with_es: Se probaron siete formas de copiar una mitad con cada hilo en los mismos dos hilos de hardware, con precarga en el propio hilo y opciones de escritura directa a memoria.
runs.faster_where_es: Para las dos permutaciones de 256 MiB con hilos que comparten núcleo, la mejor variante con precarga auxiliar tardó un 59–77 % más que la copia repartida. Frente a un único hilo copiando, fue entre 1,16× y 1,46× más rápida. La prueba mide la copia en un orden dado.

runs.title: Page reuse when real flight batches overlap
runs.summary: The 36 monthly airport pairs had more than 99% of rows in the shared time interval. Even the longest single-source stretch was shorter than one page. Selecting each input's alignment nearly doubled median reusable coverage for lightly overlapping weekly batches.
runs.model: Codex (exact model and reasoning settings not captured)
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.result: 0 eligible pages in 36 heavily interleaved pairs
closes: whole-page reuse for the measured interleaved airport pairs
opens: independent starting offsets for near-disjoint runs prepared together
runs.how: A page of input can remain in place when all its rows are still together and fit a page in the merged order. We counted such pages in batches reconstructed from the departure times of 32,735 flights.
runs.compared_with: We compared the existing page alignment with moving the start of the output and with placing each input at its own starting offset before writing it.
runs.faster_where: All 36 heavily overlapping airport pairs had zero eligible pages. For the 20 weekly pairs with any overlap, choosing both input offsets raised median reusable coverage from 48.19% to 95.83%. This measures coverage under advance knowledge of both runs.
runs.title_es: Reutilización de páginas al mezclar vuelos con horarios solapados
runs.how_es: Una página de entrada puede quedarse en su sitio si todas sus filas siguen juntas y encajan en una página del resultado. Contamos esas páginas en lotes reconstruidos con los horarios de 32.735 vuelos.
runs.compared_with_es: Comparamos la alineación habitual con desplazar el comienzo de la salida y con elegir dónde empieza cada entrada antes de escribirla.
runs.faster_where_es: Ninguno de los 36 pares de aeropuertos con fuerte solapamiento tenía páginas reutilizables. En los 20 pares semanales con algún solapamiento, elegir dónde empezar ambas entradas elevó la mediana de cobertura del 48,19 % al 95,83 %. El cálculo supone conocer de antemano el orden de ambos lotes.

runs.title: Placing both batches for page reuse during a stable merge
runs.summary: With 2% overlap, independent placement doubled reusable coverage from 49% to about 98%. The Windows implementation took 1.84–2.43 times as long as the best direct reference when producing both batches and the merged result.
runs.model: Codex (exact model and reasoning settings not captured)
runs.idea: 1. Virtual memory as a data-movement engine
runs.baseline: Fastest of split bulk merge and fused cached or streaming writers
closes: producer-side page placement with this Windows mapping path
runs.how: Two searches find the ends that stay together when merging. The producer chooses where the batches start so the program can reuse both ends as whole pages and copy the middle.
runs.compared_with: Compared with fixed alignment and with the fastest direct method that produced both separate batches and a contiguous merged output.
runs.faster_where: At 128 and 256 MiB with 2% overlap, the new placement reused about 98% of the bytes and sped up fixed remapping by 1.10–1.36×. It took 1.84–2.43 times as long as the best direct writer. Batch construction and first read dominated.
runs.title_es: Alineación de los lotes para reutilizar páginas en una mezcla estable
runs.how_es: Dos búsquedas encuentran los extremos que siguen juntos en la salida. Se elige dónde empieza cada lote para reutilizar ambos extremos por páginas y copiar el centro.
runs.compared_with_es: Se comparó con la alineación fija y con la forma directa más rápida de producir los dos lotes y una salida fusionada contigua.
runs.faster_where_es: Con 128 y 256 MiB y un 2 % de solapamiento, se reutilizó cerca del 98 % de los bytes. La aceleración frente al remapeo fijo fue de 1,10× a 1,36×. El método tardó entre 1,84 y 2,43 veces lo que tardó la mejor escritura directa. La preparación y la primera lectura concentraron el coste.
